# Coding agent replacement — M7 Slice 6

Status: experimental TypeScript engine source profile, 2026-09-10. Requires Node 24, SQLite and an existing CODING_V1 binding. This extends the [execution binding contract](./EXECUTION-BINDINGS.md) with supervised whole-agent transfer at an unstarted or fully settled stage boundary.

M10 amends this contract: agent binding §4 (not in this pack) makes agent replacement the only route to a new binding on a bound run, names a set of nodes and one successor, and adds the activation bar and reconciliation first. M10 slice 7 implements them for a run bound under readiness, replacing the agent of every node: the successor rule, a proposal that names its successor, the activation bar, and the successor's node assignment and readiness binding (record (not in this pack)). Naming a subset of nodes is slice 8. Where a sentence below states the M10 rule, the implementation's narrower behaviour is named beside it.

## Commands and authority

`ACTIVATE_REPLACEMENT` carries `ref`, `proposalId`, `expectedWorkflowRevision`, `replacement: {agentId, capabilityDigest}` and `approvalId`. A proposal names a non-empty set of nodes and one successor, and its candidate changes the agent of the named nodes only, with task identities, material, dependencies and protected policies unchanged (§4 (not in this pack)). Replacing every node is the special case of naming all of them; two successors in one proposal are refused, because that is two proposals. The successor differs from a named node's current agent in agent id or capability digest: the same agent id with a new capability digest is a valid successor, and the identical pair is refused, because that is restore, not replacement. The implementation accepts only the every-node case, with the candidate equal to `definitionWithAgentReplacement(currentDefinition, replacement)`. A proposal may name its `successor` (`{agentId, capabilityDigest}`), an additive field of `aiws-change/1`; a proposal that names it activates only that successor, and a successor with the current agent id needs it, because the definition carries agent ids only. The identical pair is refused with `SUCCESSOR_NOT_DISTINCT`, and so is the current agent id while the current capability digest is unknown, as on a run bound to the built-in local agent without a readiness binding.

The configured host must authenticate and authorize the caller, the engine must hold an exact human approval bound to the candidate, replacement material, current aggregate revision/state, action and epoch, and the host must supply `verifyReplacement(target, review)`. This independent host check runs before the command, outside any database transaction, against a fresh review. It returns a capability record as data: the exact target and capability digest, a nonempty evidence reference, an unexpired timestamp, and the `subjectDigest` of the review it verified against. Inside the write transaction the engine checks the record against the review it resolves there. A record whose `subjectDigest` differs, because the material changed between the host's verification and execution, fails with `STALE_REVISION` and commits nothing. Expiry is checked again before commit. No host code runs inside the transaction. The engine does not infer capabilities from an agent's claim. **Activation bar** (§4 (not in this pack)): before commit, for each named node, the engine evaluates readiness for the successor against the successor binding from a fresh host snapshot, with every confinement condition VERIFIED and the manifest digest matching, and runs the binding-time credential checks of §3 (not in this pack). A failure refuses activation with `READINESS_BLOCKED` or `CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`, consumes no attempt and makes no reservation, and a failure on one named node refuses the whole proposal. `verifyReplacement` evidence is still required, and dispatch rechecks everything. The runner evaluates the bar for every review, challenge and execution of the command on a run bound under readiness, against the current binding's stated requirements (the runner's minimums alone for a run bound under 1.0.0), and the review carries the result's `successorDigest`, which the approval subject binds, and `allowanceWarning`. As at binding, an agent the catalog does not offer, a model set the model register refuses and an exposure the successor's manifest does not admit are refused. A run bound without readiness has no bar beyond `verifyReplacement`. Production capability manifests and authentication are host responsibilities.

Under M10, activation writes one immutable successor assignment and readiness binding per named node, in the same transaction as the records below; on a run bound under readiness the implementation writes them for its one node, the binding stored one row per node assignment with the manifest it pins (readiness component version 3). Activation also atomically records the definition/head, one immutable whole-run assignment and its capability evidence, immutable handoff, coding state transition, superseded queue records, human decision/consumed approval, audit event and request receipt. Retries return the original receipt; competing or stale proposals cannot override the head. Failed transactions leave none of these writes visible.

`ACK_REPLACEMENT` carries `ref`, `assignmentId` and `handoffDigest`. Only an authenticated, authorized AGENT whose principal ID equals the current target can acknowledge its exact current assignment. Human activation approval is insufficient. Acknowledgment is immutable and scoped to the coordinator epoch. A restart requires a new epoch acknowledgment before new dispatch, in addition to the existing human resume procedure. The same epoch can safely retry the acknowledgment.

`HOLD_REPLACEMENT` carries `ref`, `expectedWorkflowRevision`, `reason` and `approvalId`. Exact human review authorizes an atomic immutable replacement hold, dispatch hold, HELD workflow state, audit event and receipt. No target assignment or successor graph is created by a hold.

## Boundary and responsibility

**Reconciliation first** (§4 (not in this pack)): after a failed attempt the sequence is `RECONCILE_CODING` with the host's no-effect or retry-safe proof, then `ACTIVATE_REPLACEMENT`, then the successor's acknowledgment and a fresh stage approval in either order. `HOLD_REPLACEMENT` may be opened first to freeze publication of the failed result and is optional; there is no combined command. Neither command is refused for a run bound under readiness. A node may be named only if it has no running or unsettled attempt. The implementation refuses `ACTIVATE_REPLACEMENT` with `RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED` on a run held for a reason `RECONCILE_CODING` clears, and the reconcile-then-replace stepper leads a human through the sequence from such a hold (record (not in this pack)).

Activation requires the current owner epoch, READY or AWAITING_APPROVAL state, no final acceptance/validation decision, no unsettled attempt in the coding scope, no attempt for the next stage, no active scheduler claim, RUNNING controls, and no open accounting or replacement hold. M10 keeps this boundary unchanged (§4 (not in this pack)). Any outstanding scheduler task must be the current unclaimed READY/WAITING task; any outstanding handoff must be the current PENDING handoff. Prior completed/consumed records are retained.

The exact old state is captured in a `coding-agent-handoff/1` record with the previous agent, source workflow revision, successor definition, next task ID and superseded task/handoff IDs. Its digest is pinned in the new assignment. Source state includes plan/artifact references, stage and ordinal, prior input/preparation manifests, counters and old handoff identity. This is an explicit supervisor-reviewed transfer. Renewed stage approval creates the normal planning-origin stage handoff; it does not invent an old-worker acknowledgment.

Old queued instances are explicitly CANCELED. The next task identity incorporates the unique assignment generation. The workflow enters AWAITING_APPROVAL and discards its old stage approval. Stage, ordinal, plan, scope, consumed evidence, resource accounting and correction bounds are preserved. The successor must acknowledge the handoff, and the human must approve the resulting stage before dispatch. These two actions may occur in either order.

Running or ambiguous work is not transferred. A hold blocks new bound delivery, acknowledgment and result publication while retaining attempts, unsettled exposure and evidence. It neither kills an external process nor proves that its effects stopped, and it does not settle, refund, compensate or erase responsibility. Generic resume cannot clear this hold. Slice 7 now supplies [explicit same-stage retry after verified reconciliation](./CODING-RECONCILIATION.md); unresolved effects remain held.

## Execution and history

`CodingWorkflowRunner` accepts host-installed `agentAdapters` keyed by logical agent identity. Each adapter supplies the reviewed capability digest and `execute(request)`. Dispatch fails before acquiring the stage handoff if the adapter is missing or its digest differs. The existing local worker can be wrapped for demonstration; production adapter trust and workspace isolation are outside this profile.

Worker identity includes coordinator epoch and immutable assignment ID. Task material, attempt pins and execution evidence include the target identity, capability digest, assignment ID and handoff digest. Live delivery and publication verify current assignment and definition, acknowledgment, worker ownership and hold status. Historical evidence retains its original pins; already consumed evidence is not relabeled as replacement work. Existing saved-evidence recovery remains supported under the same assignment after human restart approval; no unsettled attempt may be transferred to another assignment.

Repeated replacement is supported at eligible boundaries, including replacing a target that has not yet acknowledged. Superseded assignment acknowledgments cannot authorize current execution. Under M10, insertion on a bound run creates a node assignment for the inserted node and meets the same activation bar (§4 (not in this pack)); after an agent replacement the M7 implementation still rejects preparation insertion with `AGENT_BOUND_CHANGE_UNSUPPORTED` and plan/dependency revisions with `AGENT_REPLACEMENT_DISABLED`. A replacement touches only the replaced node's assignment, binding, task identity and inbound stage handoff, and nothing resets (§4 (not in this pack)); the M7 implementation replaces every node's agent and also resets nothing. Arbitrary branch edits, remote controls and native SDK bindings are outside this slice.

## Verification

See delivery evidence (not in this pack), [guide](../../guide/engine-agent-replacement.md) and example (not in this pack). SQLite transactions and process kills are tested locally; this does not close M6 device, platform, backup/migration or long-duration qualification gates.
